newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL short-term rates rise after bond issue payment.
newsitem.headline: KL short-term rates rise after bond issue payment.

text.p: Short-term interbank rates rose sharply after banks forked out two billion ringgit for a seven-year government bond issue, dealers said on Monday.
They said one-week interbank rates rose to 7.20/30 percent against 6.90/7.00 percent, two-week money was at 7.20/30 against 6.80/90 and one-month at 7.30/35 against 7.25/30.
Three-month money was being quoted at 7.35/40 percent against 7.30/35 and six-month unchanged at 7.35/40.
"The reserve requirement and bond issue payment are today. These two factors seem to have taken out liquidity from the system," said Jimmy Koh, analyst with research firm I.D.E.A. in Singapore.
Apart from paying for the bonds, banks also had to top up their reserve accounts with the central bank on Monday.
Banks have to maintain 13.5 percent of their deposits as reserves with the cenral bank.
The Malaysian banking system has been flush in the last few weeks due to a rash of central bank deposit maturities and overseas fund inflows.
This had kept interbank rates depressed until Friday, when banks pushed up the rates ahead of the bond issue.
"I am not sure whether all the excess liquidity is gone. I don't think so. I guess it is only a short-term mismatch," Koh of I.D.E.A said.
However, the new government bond was trading at a lower yield of 6.51/52 percent against average issue coupon of 6.586 percent and post-results yield on Friday of 6.523 percent.
